en: Mount Pinatubo's massive 1991 eruption lowered global average temperatures by about one degree Fahrenheit for several years.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the South China Sea.
The Zambales ophiolite complex contains large deposits of chromite, a hard, dark metallic mineral mined in the Philippines.
Olympus Mons, a massive shield volcano on Mars, is the tallest known mountain in our entire solar system.
Sirius, located in the Canis Major constellation, is the brightest star visible in Earth's night sky.
Apollo 11 astronauts landed on the Moon's Sea of Tranquility, marking the first human visit to another celestial body.
The Amihan, or northeast monsoon, brings cool, dry air to the Philippines between November and February every year.
The rich, dark volcanic soil around Mayon Volcano makes the local lands in Albay highly fertile for agriculture.
During an El Niño event, warmer Pacific Ocean waters cause severe droughts and water shortages across the Philippines.
Talc is the softest mineral on the Mohs hardness scale and is commonly used to make commercial baby powder.
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant, persistent storm that has been raging on the planet for centuries.
The 1990 Luzon earthquake, measuring 7.8 in magnitude, caused massive destruction and ground liquefaction in Baguio and Cabanatuan.
